Method of Attack: Malware infects computers and alters audio drivers to flip input jacks to output jacks and vice versa, weaponizing headphones and speakers as covert microphones to record audio without user consent.
Discoverer: Scientists from the Cyber-Security Research Center at the Ben-Gurion University of the Negev in Israel
Impacted Systems: Computers with Realtek audio chipsets or similar drivers allowing input/output jack switching
Indicators of Compromise: YouTube video demonstrating Speake(a)r eavesdropping attack
